Consolidated Callisto review: latest #242 and #253
2026-11-27

Assessment

#242 has corrected its earlier advisory, performance-isolation, explicit-help, README-recovery and stderr-contract findings. Its newest batching change introduces a confirmed production regression: sufficiently large prerelease history searches exceed the operating system argument limit. A separate test assumes recursive native Git tag peeling and fails under the older supported listing capability.

#253 has one current automated finding confirmed: its native Git fixture inherits configuration that can bypass its local transport route. The original environment-dump assertion is corrected, but the adjacent PATH-filtering assertion retains the same unsafe failure diagnostic. Four previously demonstrated native Git product defects remain in the code as retained base behavior. They are not newly introduced #253 regressions or automatic scope gates for the narrowed PR; they belong to the explicitly tracked remote follow-up unless the owner chooses to include them here.

A combined closure claim is premature. The immediate correction batch is four focused items, not a new general framework: stdin transport for large grep patterns, deterministic Git-capability test oracles, child-local fixture config isolation, and completion of the environment assertion cleanup.

Exact scope

#242: clean 98620363ec72bb14bbb50e97dc1d3e3b856c6e56, local wp-onboarding-friction-fix, remote change wp-onboarding-friction, PR634, trail487.
#253: clean 0b219304c7dfbf150e761ee4e0a8167fe4961196, local wp-git-boundary-split, remote change wp-git-boundary, PR645, trail494.
Both heads contain #246's reviewed 0992460d76b2825bec963c9dbac44a702097b84e. The old integration worktree is no longer evidence that #246's correction is absent from these branches. A final combination of #242 and #253 has not been built or gated in this review.
The captured source and final worktree comparison match. See 242-manifest.json, 253-manifest.json and final-state.json. No actual worktree edits, commits, remote comments, resolutions, pushes, PR closures or merges were performed.

Current corrections required

1. #242, medium: prerelease historical-name search can fail E2BIG.
Finding 01M8D7MKK8P6GGRNBKBFXFJY05.
Locations: model vcs/access.rs:439-445; graph history.rs:67-72; graph lib.rs:353-359,434-442.
PreJsonOrigin registers all historical baseline names; the first fallback ownership search puts every name in argv as -e/name. A moved manifest and a current shared bare name force sole_owner_at, which propagates process-spawn failure to version. This is not merely a direct helper called with synthetic unsupported inputs.
Full latest CLI reproduction: small control exits0 and plans cargo/foo 1.0.0 to1.0.1-alpha.0. The same moved/shared-name case with8831 additional historical baseline keys exits1/E024 with Argument list too long (os error7). The fixture pre.json is1,757,456 bytes; estimated pattern argv1,677,897 bytes; native ARG_MAX1,048,576. See lane242/reproduce_e2big.py and e2big-results.json.
Correction: keep one Git process, send patterns through existing CommandRunner::run_with_stdin and git grep -l -z -F -i -f - <rev> -- <pathspecs>. Preserve no-needles behavior, exit1=no-match, other failures, fixed-string case-insensitive semantics, and NUL pathname framing. A native stdin control already searches the same8832 names successfully and finds old-crate/Cargo.toml; this validates the transport direction, not an implemented CLI fix.
Complete migration: graph history::CountingGrep and model access test RealGit implement run but not real stdin handling; migrate their delegation and process counting with the production helper. FakeRunner currently discards stdin, so add an actual payload oracle. Default run_with_stdin is Unsupported; do not mistake that for a harmless fallback. If compatibility with run-only third-party runners is a requirement, handle specifically Unsupported with byte-bounded batches rather than swallowing arbitrary command failures. No new trait, async runtime, dependency or error code is required.
Validation: large/small full CLI must yield the same cargo bump; exact payload is on stdin rather than argv; existing literal/case/no-match/empty/invalid-ref behavior and constant process tests remain meaningful. Avoid a routine unit oracle tied to one machine's ARG_MAX.

2. #242, low: performance positive control depends on native Git peeling capability.
Finding 01M8D7MKKQB9QH8GN8P1ZS8C4P.
Location: cli tests/git_process_count_tests.rs:238-239.
The false branch disables the compatibility shim but uses whatever Git is on PATH. It does not establish recursive peeling of nested annotated tags. When the listing returns an inner tag, resumption legitimately starts fallback rev-parse processes and the unconditional equality assertion fails.
Evidence: the exact current test executable passes with native Git. Under an accurate single-level listing shim, the positive-control test fails101 with counts[9,13]; the historical-tag pending-hint test still passes. See lane242/reproduce_legacy_git_test.py and legacy-git-test-results.json. This is a test portability defect, not recurrence of the production pending-hint issue. No precise Git-version threshold is inferred from emulation.
Correction: control both recursive and single-level listing responses, or probe native peel capability and gate only the matching native assertion. Compute shim oracle data before counted execution. Keep the historical-tag Auto/Changeset comparisons, legacy positive control and aggregate cache-miss/active controls. Do not introduce an undeclared minimum Git version.

3. #253, low: native fixture is not isolated from inherited Git config.
Finding 01M8D42239XRCNG4G6K9KB1J7C.
Location: graph commands/release/provider/tag/native_remote_tests.rs:24-30; shared fixture GitRunner/run_git setup and invocation paths.
The fixture injects a file redirect only for an HTTPS prefix, and only for push/ls-remote. A global insteadOf rule changes the URL during get-url; preparation produces SSH and the redirect no longer matches. The test can attempt GitHub access and fail or wait instead of using its bare repository.
Evidence: a synthetic global rewrite plus a local SSH canary demonstrates the escaped argv without opening a socket. The actual compiled Rust test also fails101 under that config and passes0 when global config is isolated. The first unscaled run timed out after25seconds in observation retry; bounded repetitions used the existing test sleep scale0. See 253-fixture-tests.json, its logs and lane253/fixture-isolation-results.json.
Correction: isolate global/system and command-injected config for every child of this fixture, from setup through preparation, observation, push and verification. Use child-local command environments, not process-global environment mutation in parallel tests. Preserve deliberate repository-local config used to exercise native behavior. Do not solve a test fixture problem by restricting production users' Git configuration or adding another URL-prefix special case.

4. #253, low, previously reported sibling: raw environment is still printed on assertion failure.
Location: cli runner.rs:650-665, run_with_timeout_env_filtered_removes_named_variables.
The original every_git_child_gets_the_git_environment assertion now names only the failed expected setting; prior normal/fault-injected tests demonstrated that correction. The adjacent PATH-removal test still runs /usr/bin/env and interpolates its whole stdout if filtering fails. That can disclose unrelated inherited variables in failure logs. It is test-only; no actual secret exposure is claimed.
Correction: give this assertion a static diagnostic too. Prefer probes that return only the requested checks. Complete both failure paths in one batch; extending a secret-name list is not a general substitute. The earlier claim that no other test prints an environment was not supported by this sibling.

Earlier issues now closed

#242 advisory output: one shared best-effort sink preserves success, E169 and usage/error exits; required decision/prompt output remains fallible.
Original pending-hint performance/test isolation: inactive inference guard and explicit cache-miss/active controls remain. Historical-version Auto/Changeset comparisons isolate the hint. The new native-capability finding above is separate.
Explicit help: common stdout sink now handles explicit help, parser help/version and completions; closed streams and non-BrokenPipe behavior are covered.
README recovery: README is written before the config initialization marker. A permission-failure/retry test proves no config remains and plain init completes after permissions are repaired. This is not a claim of multi-file transactions.
Stderr documentation: the contract now distinguishes optional notes/echo/error rendering from required prompts and init review. JSON init can still refuse when mandatory review output fails; that behavior no longer contradicts the policy.
#246: duplicate detection and explicit rows-only policy are integrated in both heads. Numeric strings in hazardous lists remain row syntax. The previous claim that all hazardous-name text is rejected was too broad; that does not make the announced owner-selected row grammar incorrect.
#253 original !env failure diagnostic: corrected. Its sibling above remains distinct.

Four retained native Git product defects: confirmed, separately deferred

The latest binding.rs/provider/tag.rs production paths are unchanged from the prior counterexamples. On latest source,22 existing provider tests pass and the four extra desired-behavior tests fail in a disposable copy, using private local repositories:
- Rewrite twice, high: get-url resolves A-to-B; passing B back to Git resolves B-to-C. Observation and publishing can use a repository different from native origin.
- First push URL only, high: later required destinations never enter observation, publication, confirmation or binding. First Exact can adopt an incomplete release.
- Transport path reconstructed from forge identity, high: accepted SSH repo is rewritten to repo.git even when they are distinct repositories.
- Ambient followTags, medium: an explicit planned-tag refspec can still publish unrelated annotated tags when push.followTags=true.
See 253-provider.log and source253-adversarial test additions. These are current product facts, not a claim that the latest narrow PR introduced them.

The remote follow-up needs a coherent distinction between exact native transport data, resolved destination set, and optional forge identity. Preserve native rewrite-once and all required push destinations; observations must correspond to the same destinations as effects. Passing origin to every ls-remote is insufficient because that reads the fetch side. Normalize only the intended tag effect with --no-follow-tags; preserve user-selected routing. Do not introduce destination authorization, an allowlist or broad production config suppression.

Disposition of the five old remote.rs review findings

Fetch-versus-push and promisor parser paths were removed with the proposed abstraction and restored base behavior; broader binding work is deferred. URLless origin is refused by the current parser even when get-url prints origin and exits0. Remaining CR/LF in the first push URL is refused before effects, rather than supported losslessly. Direct endpoint pushing avoids remote.origin.mirror. These are removed/deferred/narrow corrections, not proof that every native transport semantic is now correct. Keep the four counterexamples attached to the remote spike instead of reopening deleted-code IDs or claiming the base defects are fixed.

Why review keeps finding more

The process-count optimization moved unbounded data into argv: fewer subprocesses alone is not a resource bound. Both new fixture findings rely on uncontrolled external prerequisites: Git capability and inherited configuration. The raw-env sibling shows a one-line correction without completing the same-pattern sweep. Review status has also mixed actual corrections, deleted paths and intentional scope deferrals. A clean reviewer pass on one host cannot replace these missing oracles.

Execution and limits

Latest #242 CLI build exited0. Focused latest tests:6 closed-stream,10 Git-process,1 init-recovery and3 history tests pass. Full CLI E2BIG red/control and native-capability red/control are independently recorded. Latest #253 provider run exits101:22 existing tests pass and4 added provider counterexamples fail. The inherited-config exact-test red/control is101/0, with network blocked by a canary. Full readiness pipeline, final integrated #242+#253 behavior, broad benchmarks and all supported-platform matrices were not run here. All started checks finished or their timeout is explicitly recorded. Brain brief failed due its local lock permissions; current source and Entire review records supplied the evidence.

Closure sequence

Fix the four scoped items above in complete boundary-sized batches. Re-run the supplied counterexamples and their controls after each correction. Keep the fixed findings closed unless a concrete counterexample defeats their current contract. Ensure the separate remote follow-up retains all four product counterexamples and truthful scope. Build/gate the actual final combination of #242 and #253; run the required repository readiness commands at its final commits. No result here guarantees all possible repository bugs have been found.
